questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Commerce is defined as the study of how

options.A: man utilizes the resources in his physical environment
options.B: man produces, distributes and consumes his goods and services
options.C: man buys, sells and distributes goods and services
options.D: raw materials are changed into finished goods.

questions.ai_explanation: Commerce concerns buying, selling and distributing goods and services, including activities that support exchange. Production and consumption together describe a wider field of economic activity.
questions.explanation: Commerce concerns buying, selling and distributing goods and services, including activities that support exchange. Production and consumption together describe a wider field of economic activity.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The type of activity which turns processed raw materials into consumer and industrial goods is described as
questions.ai_explanation: Manufacturing transforms processed materials into finished goods for consumers or industry. Extraction obtains natural resources, while construction assembles structures such as roads and buildings.
questions.explanation: Manufacturing transforms processed materials into finished goods for consumers or industry. Extraction obtains natural resources, while construction assembles structures such as roads and buildings.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Which of the following takes place when firms producing at different stages in the same industry combine?
questions.ai_explanation: Vertical integration joins businesses at different stages of the same supply chain, such as a producer and its distributor. Horizontal integration combines businesses at the same stage.
questions.explanation: Vertical integration joins businesses at different stages of the same supply chain, such as a producer and its distributor. Horizontal integration combines businesses at the same stage.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Among the following groups, whose claims rank ahead of shareholders when a company is liquidated?
questions.ai_explanation: Debenture holders lend money to the company and have creditor claims. These claims rank ahead of distributions to owners, including preference and ordinary shareholders.
questions.explanation: Debenture holders lend money to the company and have creditor claims. These claims rank ahead of distributions to owners, including preference and ordinary shareholders.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Compulsory dissolution of a business can arise from

options.B: A declaration by a court of law

questions.ai_explanation: Compulsory winding up is imposed through a court order. An agreement by the owners is voluntary, while poor economic conditions alone do not constitute a legal dissolution order.
questions.explanation: Compulsory winding up is imposed through a court order. An agreement by the owners is voluntary, while poor economic conditions alone do not constitute a legal dissolution order.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: MBV balances: fittings ₦9,200; vehicles ₦7,500; stock ₦8,800; debtors ₦15,500; bank ₦21,000; cash ₦6,380; creditors ₦9,730. Opening capital ₦60,000, net profit ₦5,250 and drawings ₦6,600. Find circulating capital (current assets).
questions.ai_explanation: Circulating capital means current assets here. Add stock ₦8,800, debtors ₦15,500, bank ₦21,000 and cash ₦6,380 to obtain ₦51,680; fixed fittings and vehicles are excluded.
questions.explanation: Circulating capital means current assets here. Add stock ₦8,800, debtors ₦15,500, bank ₦21,000 and cash ₦6,380 to obtain ₦51,680; fixed fittings and vehicles are excluded.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: What are fixtures and fittings in a balance sheet?
questions.ai_explanation: Fixtures and fittings are kept for continuing use in running the business. They are therefore fixed assets, rather than inventory, liquid funds or the net working-capital balance.
questions.explanation: Fixtures and fittings are kept for continuing use in running the business. They are therefore fixed assets, rather than inventory, liquid funds or the net working-capital balance.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Governments impose import duties for the following reasons EXCEPT which?

options.A: To raise revenue for other services
options.B: To act as a retaliatory measure against other governments
options.C: To discourage the redistribution of income at home
options.D: To protect home industries from external competition

questions.ai_explanation: Import duties can raise public revenue, protect domestic producers or respond to another country’s trade restrictions. Discouraging domestic income redistribution is not a standard purpose of such duties.
questions.explanation: Import duties can raise public revenue, protect domestic producers or respond to another country’s trade restrictions. Discouraging domestic income redistribution is not a standard purpose of such duties.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Sole enterprise may flourish best in
questions.ai_explanation: A small retail business can be managed directly by one owner and commonly needs less capital than mining, oil exploration or vehicle assembly. This makes retailing the most suitable listed example.
questions.explanation: A small retail business can be managed directly by one owner and commonly needs less capital than mining, oil exploration or vehicle assembly. This makes retailing the most suitable listed example.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The use of coin-operated machines to sell goods is a form of
questions.ai_explanation: A vending machine sells goods directly to the final consumer. That is retailing, even though the transaction uses a machine rather than a shop assistant or personal sales visit.
questions.explanation: A vending machine sells goods directly to the final consumer. That is retailing, even though the transaction uses a machine rather than a shop assistant or personal sales visit.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: What is the major function of the wholesaler?

options.A: Buying from small-scale producers and selling to exporters.
options.B: Buying in bulk and selling in small quantities
options.C: Granting of credit facilities to retailers
options.D: Providing information to manufacturers on market situation.

questions.ai_explanation: Wholesalers buy large quantities and divide them into smaller lots for retailers. Credit and market information may support this role, but bulk buying and breaking bulk are its central trading function.
questions.explanation: Wholesalers buy large quantities and divide them into smaller lots for retailers. Credit and market information may support this role, but bulk buying and breaking bulk are its central trading function.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The rate at which a country’s exports exchange for its imports is called
questions.ai_explanation: Terms of trade compare export prices with import prices. They describe how much imports a country can obtain for its exports, rather than the monetary trade balance.
questions.explanation: Terms of trade compare export prices with import prices. They describe how much imports a country can obtain for its exports, rather than the monetary trade balance.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The difference between the value of a country’s exports and imports within a given period is called what?
questions.ai_explanation: The balance of trade compares export receipts with import expenditure. The balance of payments is broader, also recording international income, transfers and financial transactions.
questions.explanation: The balance of trade compares export receipts with import expenditure. The balance of payments is broader, also recording international income, transfers and financial transactions.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Which department immediately preceded the Nigerian Postal Service in the 1985 reorganisation?
questions.ai_explanation: Before the 1985 reorganisation, Posts and Telecommunications combined postal and telecommunications functions. Its postal division became NIPOST while the telecommunications operations were reorganised separately.
questions.explanation: Before the 1985 reorganisation, Posts and Telecommunications combined postal and telecommunications functions. Its postal division became NIPOST while the telecommunications operations were reorganised separately.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Goods discharged from ships on which import duties have not been paid are kept in the
questions.ai_explanation: A bonded warehouse holds imported goods under customs control while duties remain unpaid. Storage there postpones duty payment until the goods are released under the applicable customs procedure.
questions.explanation: A bonded warehouse holds imported goods under customs control while duties remain unpaid. Storage there postpones duty payment until the goods are released under the applicable customs procedure.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: One of the effects of the devaluation of the Naira is that the

options.A: goods that can be imported with the Naira have become cheaper
options.B: value of other currencies relative to the Naira have become cheaper
options.C: goods that can be exported from Nigeria have become costlier
options.D: imports that can be bought with the Naira have become costlier.

questions.ai_explanation: Devaluation lowers the domestic currency’s value relative to foreign currencies. With foreign prices unchanged, more naira are needed for the same imported goods, making imports costlier in naira.
questions.explanation: Devaluation lowers the domestic currency’s value relative to foreign currencies. With foreign prices unchanged, more naira are needed for the same imported goods, making imports costlier in naira.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The financial institution established to boost Nigeria’s trade with the rest of the world is called
questions.ai_explanation: NEXIM is Nigeria’s export-import bank. Its export financing and risk-bearing services support Nigerian trade, unlike deposit insurance or institutions focused primarily on industrial development.
questions.explanation: NEXIM is Nigeria’s export-import bank. Its export financing and risk-bearing services support Nigerian trade, unlike deposit insurance or institutions focused primarily on industrial development.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The elements of the marketing mix are
questions.ai_explanation: The traditional marketing mix consists of product, price, place and promotion. These cover what is offered, what customers pay, how it reaches them and how it is communicated.
questions.explanation: The traditional marketing mix consists of product, price, place and promotion. These cover what is offered, what customers pay, how it reaches them and how it is communicated.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Which of the following items has the shortest effect on the consumer?
questions.ai_explanation: A fad rises and fades quickly, so its influence on consumers is short-lived. Fashion generally lasts longer, while an innovation may create a durable change in products or behaviour.
questions.explanation: A fad rises and fades quickly, so its influence on consumers is short-lived. Fashion generally lasts longer, while an innovation may create a durable change in products or behaviour.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Which of the following is a form of sales promotion?
questions.ai_explanation: Free samples are a sales-promotion incentive that lets consumers try a product. Radio and television advertising communicate a message but do not themselves give the customer a trial sample.
questions.explanation: Free samples are a sales-promotion incentive that lets consumers try a product. Radio and television advertising communicate a message but do not themselves give the customer a trial sample.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: One advantage of personal selling over all other elements of promotion is that

options.B: it is very cheap in terms of cost per contract
options.C: it does not need to use mass media

questions.ai_explanation: Personal selling allows two-way conversation. The seller can hear objections or questions immediately and respond on the spot, giving faster direct feedback than one-way advertising.
questions.explanation: Personal selling allows two-way conversation. The seller can hear objections or questions immediately and respond on the spot, giving faster direct feedback than one-way advertising.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: An agreement to sell differs from a sale because, in the former, the transfer of ownership of goods is what?
questions.ai_explanation: An agreement to sell postpones the transfer of ownership until a future time or condition. A completed sale transfers ownership, although physical delivery may occur at a different time.
questions.explanation: An agreement to sell postpones the transfer of ownership until a future time or condition. A completed sale transfers ownership, although physical delivery may occur at a different time.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Amusa offers to sell Bello a hat for ₦30. Bello replies, “I will pay ₦29.” Which describes the exchange?
questions.ai_explanation: The offer is to sell for ₦30. Replying with ₦29 proposes a different price, so it is a counter-offer rather than acceptance of the original terms. The exchange has not formed an agreed bargain.
questions.explanation: The offer is to sell for ₦30. Replying with ₦29 proposes a different price, so it is a counter-offer rather than acceptance of the original terms. The exchange has not formed an agreed bargain.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Nationalization of an industry means that its ownership becomes that of
questions.ai_explanation: Nationalisation transfers an industry or enterprise into government ownership. It differs from indigenisation, which concerns ownership by nationals rather than necessarily by the state.
questions.explanation: Nationalisation transfers an industry or enterprise into government ownership. It differs from indigenisation, which concerns ownership by nationals rather than necessarily by the state.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: NACCIMA stands for

options.A: Nigerian-American Centre for Culture Industries, Mines and Arts
options.B: Nigerian Association for Culture, Civics, Industries, Minerals and Arts
options.C: National Agency for Culture, Civilization, Investments, Manufacturing and Agriculture
options.D: Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture

questions.ai_explanation: NACCIMA brings together chambers representing commerce, industry, mining and agriculture. Its name identifies this business-chamber association, rather than a cultural agency or government investment body.
questions.explanation: NACCIMA brings together chambers representing commerce, industry, mining and agriculture. Its name identifies this business-chamber association, rather than a cultural agency or government investment body.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The harmonious relationship among the various units in an organization is ensured through
questions.ai_explanation: Coordination links the work of different departments so their actions support shared objectives. It helps prevent conflicting schedules, duplicated effort and gaps between organisational units.
questions.explanation: Coordination links the work of different departments so their actions support shared objectives. It helps prevent conflicting schedules, duplicated effort and gaps between organisational units.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The principle of span of control stipulates which of the following?

options.A: an employee should report to only one superior
options.B: managers must demand accountability from their subordinates
options.C: resources have to be economized within the various divisions
options.D: the number of employees reporting to one superior should be kept to a workable maximum.

questions.ai_explanation: Span of control is the number of subordinates directly supervised by one manager. Keeping that number manageable supports effective supervision; reporting to one boss is unity of command.
questions.explanation: Span of control is the number of subordinates directly supervised by one manager. Keeping that number manageable supports effective supervision; reporting to one boss is unity of command.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The use of computers in modern banking industry is a reflection of
questions.ai_explanation: Computers apply technical inventions to process information and deliver banking services. Their use therefore directly illustrates technological development, even though it can also affect competition and the economy.
questions.explanation: Computers apply technical inventions to process information and deliver banking services. Their use therefore directly illustrates technological development, even though it can also affect competition and the economy.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: When an oil exploring and mining company builds a health centre in one of the communities where it operates, such a company is

options.B: Finding a way to spend excess profits
options.C: Fulfilling part of its social responsibility

questions.ai_explanation: Providing a health centre benefits the community in which the business operates. It is an example of corporate social responsibility because it supports community welfare beyond the company’s core production activity.
questions.explanation: Providing a health centre benefits the community in which the business operates. It is an example of corporate social responsibility because it supports community welfare beyond the company’s core production activity.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The Lake Chad Basin Commission was founded to enable member states.

options.A: Expand the volume of water in the lake for fishing activity
options.B: Increase navigational activities on the lake
options.C: Dam the lake for electricity and agricultural purposes
options.D: Coordinate their efforts in managing the use of the lake’s resources

questions.ai_explanation: The commission provides a framework for member countries to cooperate in managing shared lake and basin resources. Its purpose is broader than increasing navigation or building a particular dam.
questions.explanation: The commission provides a framework for member countries to cooperate in managing shared lake and basin resources. Its purpose is broader than increasing navigation or building a particular dam.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: In which of the following sets of occupations can an industrial worker be found?
questions.ai_explanation: Manufacturing makes products, extraction obtains natural resources and construction builds structures. All three are industrial activities; banking, insurance and commerce provide services supporting economic exchange.
questions.explanation: Manufacturing makes products, extraction obtains natural resources and construction builds structures. All three are industrial activities; banking, insurance and commerce provide services supporting economic exchange.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Construction activities include the building of houses and roads as well as
questions.ai_explanation: Bricklaying creates walls and other parts of buildings, making it a construction activity. Shoemaking, blacksmithing and car assembly instead manufacture or work on movable products.
questions.explanation: Bricklaying creates walls and other parts of buildings, making it a construction activity. Shoemaking, blacksmithing and car assembly instead manufacture or work on movable products.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Under the default Partnership Act 1890 rule, if partners have not agreed how to share profits, how are profits shared?

options.A: in the ratio of the value of business secured by each partner for the partnership
options.B: in the ratio of partners’ capital contributions
options.C: in an equal proportion, irrespective of partners’ capital contributions
options.D: according to duties performed by each partner.

questions.ai_explanation: Under the default Partnership Act rule, partners share profits equally unless they agree otherwise. Unequal capital contributions do not by themselves replace that equal-sharing rule.
questions.explanation: Under the default Partnership Act rule, partners share profits equally unless they agree otherwise. Unequal capital contributions do not by themselves replace that equal-sharing rule.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: In the traditional memorandum-and-articles framework, which listed information concerns internal governance in the articles of association?
questions.ai_explanation: Articles set rules for the company’s internal governance, including directors’ responsibilities and procedures. The traditional memorandum describes its constitutional objects, capital and liability framework.
questions.explanation: Articles set rules for the company’s internal governance, including directors’ responsibilities and procedures. The traditional memorandum describes its constitutional objects, capital and liability framework.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The merger of two companies producing the same type of products is an example of
questions.ai_explanation: Combining companies making the same type of product at the same stage is horizontal integration. A vertical merger instead links different stages such as manufacturing and distribution.
questions.explanation: Combining companies making the same type of product at the same stage is horizontal integration. A vertical merger instead links different stages such as manufacturing and distribution.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: One of the implications of the incorporation of a company is that

options.A: it is more difficult for the company to raise loans
options.B: the company can sue but cannot be sued
options.C: the company’s property becomes distinguished from that of its member
options.D: its members become liable for all the debts of the company.

questions.ai_explanation: Incorporation establishes a legal entity distinct from its members. Company property belongs to that entity rather than directly to the shareholders, and the company can both sue and be sued.
questions.explanation: Incorporation establishes a legal entity distinct from its members. Company property belongs to that entity rather than directly to the shareholders, and the company can both sue and be sued.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The main advantage of a sole trader is the freedom to

options.D: plough all the profits back into the business.

questions.ai_explanation: A sole trader does not need partner or board agreement for routine business choices. That concentrated control allows quick decisions, although the owner must also bear responsibility for them.
questions.explanation: A sole trader does not need partner or board agreement for routine business choices. That concentrated control allows quick decisions, although the owner must also bear responsibility for them.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: When a company uses more of loans than equity to finance its business, the company is said to be
questions.ai_explanation: Gearing compares debt finance with owners’ equity. Heavy reliance on loans gives high gearing and greater debt-service commitments, but it does not automatically mean the business is bankrupt.
questions.explanation: Gearing compares debt finance with owners’ equity. Heavy reliance on loans gives high gearing and greater debt-service commitments, but it does not automatically mean the business is bankrupt.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The financial index which compares current assets directly with current liabilities is known as current
questions.ai_explanation: The current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities. It compares short-term resources with short-term obligations; it is a ratio rather than a money balance.
questions.explanation: The current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities. It compares short-term resources with short-term obligations; it is a ratio rather than a money balance.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Rights issue means the

options.A: issue of shares to the directors of a company on favourable terms
options.B: issue of shares by a company only to the founders of the company
options.C: right of shareholders to vote on any issue
options.D: issue of shares to shareholders on favourable terms.

questions.ai_explanation: A rights issue offers existing shareholders the opportunity to buy additional shares, commonly at a favourable subscription price. It concerns new capital, not merely voting rights or an offer only to directors.
questions.explanation: A rights issue offers existing shareholders the opportunity to buy additional shares, commonly at a favourable subscription price. It concerns new capital, not merely voting rights or an offer only to directors.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Opening stock ₦40,000; purchases ₦115,000; closing stock ₦60,000; sales ₦250,000. Find cost of goods sold.
questions.ai_explanation: Goods available cost opening stock ₦40,000 plus purchases ₦115,000 = ₦155,000. Deduct closing stock ₦60,000 to obtain cost of goods sold of ₦95,000.
questions.explanation: Goods available cost opening stock ₦40,000 plus purchases ₦115,000 = ₦155,000. Deduct closing stock ₦60,000 to obtain cost of goods sold of ₦95,000.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: In the channel of distribution, which of the following sets is entirely made up of middlemen?
questions.ai_explanation: Wholesalers, retailers and agents act between producers and final buyers in distribution. Manufacturers create the goods and consumers use them, so those two groups are not middlemen.
questions.explanation: Wholesalers, retailers and agents act between producers and final buyers in distribution. Manufacturers create the goods and consumers use them, so those two groups are not middlemen.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Goods imported into a country for the purpose of reexporting attracts a rebate known as
questions.ai_explanation: Customs drawback is repayment of qualifying import duties when the relevant goods are subsequently exported. It is a duty-refund mechanism rather than an export royalty paid for resource rights.
questions.explanation: Customs drawback is repayment of qualifying import duties when the relevant goods are subsequently exported. It is a duty-refund mechanism rather than an export royalty paid for resource rights.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: RRF as a scheme introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria means
questions.ai_explanation: RRF expands to Refinancing and Rediscounting Facility. The name describes financing support through refinancing and rediscounting, rather than bookkeeping, recording or reinvestment.
questions.explanation: RRF expands to Refinancing and Rediscounting Facility. The name describes financing support through refinancing and rediscounting, rather than bookkeeping, recording or reinvestment.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Freight note is a document

options.A: used by government to transport goods from one country to another
options.B: issued by a shipping company giving details of charges
options.C: used for payment for imported goods.
options.D: given by an importer to pay for goods at a future period.

questions.ai_explanation: A freight note sets out the carrier’s transport charges. It concerns payment for carriage, rather than the purchase price of the goods or a promise by the importer to pay the supplier later.
questions.explanation: A freight note sets out the carrier’s transport charges. It concerns payment for carriage, rather than the purchase price of the goods or a promise by the importer to pay the supplier later.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: An invoice for ₦600 allows discounts of 5% within one month, 2½% within three months and 1% within five months. How much is payable if settled in the second month?
questions.ai_explanation: Payment in month two falls after the one-month 5% deadline but within the three-month 2½% period. Discount is ₦600 × 0.025 = ₦15, leaving ₦585 payable.
questions.explanation: Payment in month two falls after the one-month 5% deadline but within the three-month 2½% period. Discount is ₦600 × 0.025 = ₦15, leaving ₦585 payable.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Spot market goods are those which are available for
questions.ai_explanation: A spot transaction concerns goods available for immediate or prompt delivery. A forward transaction instead agrees delivery at a future date, so long-term or year-end delivery is not the defining feature.
questions.explanation: A spot transaction concerns goods available for immediate or prompt delivery. A forward transaction instead agrees delivery at a future date, so long-term or year-end delivery is not the defining feature.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The main advantage of road transport is that it is
questions.ai_explanation: Road transport can change routes and reach individual premises, giving flexible door-to-door service. Its cost, speed and safety depend on the journey, so those are not universal advantages.
questions.explanation: Road transport can change routes and reach individual premises, giving flexible door-to-door service. Its cost, speed and safety depend on the journey, so those are not universal advantages.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: An insurer accepts a large risk and then shares part of that risk with other insurers. What is this called?
questions.ai_explanation: Reinsurance transfers part of an insurer’s accepted risk to another insurer. It helps spread exposure to large claims; contribution instead concerns overlapping policies covering the same loss.
questions.explanation: Reinsurance transfers part of an insurer’s accepted risk to another insurer. It helps spread exposure to large claims; contribution instead concerns overlapping policies covering the same loss.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: Berne Union is also known as

options.C: International Union of Credit and Investment Insurers

questions.ai_explanation: The Berne Union is the International Union of Credit and Investment Insurers. Its members work in export-credit and investment insurance, rather than forming a consumer credit union.
questions.explanation: The Berne Union is the International Union of Credit and Investment Insurers. Its members work in export-credit and investment insurance, rather than forming a consumer credit union.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.question: The breaking down of a market into separate and identifiable elements each with its own special product requirements is known as market
questions.ai_explanation: Market segmentation divides potential customers into identifiable groups with different needs or characteristics. This enables products and marketing efforts to be tailored to each group.
questions.explanation: Market segmentation divides potential customers into identifiable groups with different needs or characteristics. This enables products and marketing efforts to be tailored to each group.
